blind_spots_patched: Baseline Chapters 1-6 completely omitted TARIL's regulatory compliance sanctions (World Bank Sanctions Case No. 788 and 2023 GETCO stop-deal notice), rapid departures of both external professional CEOs, early-2025 ₹750 Cr enabling QIP approval, and sharp institutional ownership attrition.

Baseline Chapter 4 named peers generically without documenting the synchronized 2025-2028 industry capacity expansion wave from multinational incumbents and IPO-bound domestic rivals responding to peak scarcity pricing.

Baseline Chapters 3 and 6 did not incorporate the Sep 30, 2026 H1 FY27 consolidated balance-sheet expansion in borrowings, CWIP, and Other Assets or management's Q1 FY27 disclosure of deliberate raw-material pre-stocking through December 2026.
assumptions_changed: WEAKENED: FY26 borrowings rose to bridge negative ₹105.38 Cr CFO and working-capital expansion; net debt and liquidity trajectory during capacity expansion remained to be established.
WEAKENED: TARIL possesses an accumulated engineering and customer-qualification moat across PGCIL, NTPC, GETCO, and export utilities based on 18,000+ installations up to 1,200 kV.
CONFIRMED: Unexecuted order book rebuilt to ₹7,237 Cr at Sep 30, 2026 with ₹1,169 Cr Q2 FY27 inflow and improved Q2 FY27 margins, while working capital remains the key watch item.
